intro: An Encumbrance Certificate is the transaction history of a property. It shows, transaction by transaction, who registered what against the property — every sale deed, gift deed, mortgage and release — over the period you request.

Before you buy, before a bank lends, and before any dispute, the EC is the document everyone asks for first. JaaGa retrieves the certified EC extract for any property in Hyderabad and greater Telangana without you visiting a Sub-Registrar Office.

whenNeeded.heading: When You Need an EC
paragraphs: You need an EC before purchasing any property, to confirm the seller's ownership and check for registered mortgages. Most banks require a 13-year or 30-year EC as part of loan sanction.
You also need it when applying for a loan against property, settling an inheritance, or clearing a title objection raised during a sale.

faqs.q: What is an Encumbrance Certificate?
faqs.a: It is an official record of all registered transactions — sales, mortgages, gifts, partitions — recorded against a property for a chosen period, issued by the state Registration department.

faqs.q: How many years of EC do I need?
faqs.a: For a purchase, 13 years is standard; many banks and cautious buyers ask for 30 years. For inheritance or dispute matters, longer periods help. We can pull any period.

faqs.q: Does a clean EC guarantee clear title?
faqs.a: No. An EC only reflects registered transactions. Unregistered claims, court cases or family disputes may not appear — which is why an EC is paired with a title verification report.

CERSAI is the national registry created to close exactly this gap. JaaGa runs a CERSAI search so you know whether any lender has an active charge on the property.

faqs.q: What is CERSAI?
faqs.a: The Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest — a national registry where lenders record mortgages and charges on property.

faqs.q: Why isn't the mortgage in the EC?
faqs.a: Equitable mortgages are created by depositing title deeds without registering a mortgage deed at the SRO, so they may not reflect in the EC. CERSAI captures them.

faqs.q: Should I do both EC and CERSAI?
faqs.a: Yes. They cover different risks — the EC covers registered transactions, CERSAI covers lenders' security interests. Together they give a fuller picture.

faqs.q: Can a closed loan still show?
faqs.a: Sometimes the charge isn't marked satisfied even after repayment. We help identify and resolve this.

faqs.q: Can NRIs use this service?
